doc.title: Tom Baker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Upcoming travel plans, Spiegle Willcox and closing thanks
summary: Baker outlines his trip to New York and Europe, they chat about Spiegle Willcox, Benny Waters and the Arbors party, and the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well I want to thank you for joining us today. It’s been a pleasure. And I wish you the best. You are traveling straight back to Australia or are you here for a while?

No, I’m actually going on the train, on Monday, with Dan Barrett to New York, and we’re going to hang out as they say, and we’re meeting Bob Barnard on Tuesday night, and then I have to fly to Europe for two or three weeks worth of gigs over there. I’ve been going to Europe every year for almost twenty years, playing with Dutch bands. There’s a couple of bands that don’t have trumpet players — Dixieland bands.
Did you ever run into Spiegle Willcox over there?
I met him once. Yeah.
Yeah? He lives not too far from us and is still doing well at 93 or so. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -16-
Where does he live?
He lives in Cincinnatus, New York, which is an hour and a half south of — it’s right in the middle of New York State. He’s got a beautiful home. Cool guy.
How old is he now? Like 90 or something?
He’s definitely over 90.
I wonder if he’s as old as Benny Waters.
I think Benny Waters is 94, and I think he’s tops.
94. Right. I’m doing a festival with Dan Barrett and some Dutchmen next March. That’s the next time I’ll be in the States. The Arbors Jazz Party.
Yes. We’re thinking of going there.
Yeah. In Florida, Clearwater Bay, Clearwater Beach? Yeah, I’ll be there, we’ll see you there.
Good folks that run that thing, too.
Yeah, Mat Domber, the head of the records. I spoke to him on the phone, sounds like a good cat.
He is.
Right.
Well thanks for your time. I hope you have good music tonight.
Thanks for having us, Monk.
Okay. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -17-
